arxiv-2212-01285.description: Abstract Financial institutions manage operational risk (OpRisk) by carrying out activities required by regulation, such as collecting loss data, calculating capital requirements, and reporting. For this purpose, for each OpRisk event, loss amounts, dates, organizational units involved, event types, and descriptions are recorded in the OpRisk databases.

arxiv-2507-06663.title: Sustainability Transitions and “Bending the Curve of Biodiversity Collapse” in the Amazon Forest
arxiv-2507-06663.creator: O.Y. Romero-Goyeneche, M. Ramirez, A.M. Osorio, U. Harman-Canalle
arxiv-2507-06663.description: Abstract Abstract This paper undertakes an analysis of deforestation in the Amazon area using a pathways-based approach to sustainability. We ground the analysis primarily in the sustainability transitions literature but also draw a bridge with socio-ecological concepts which helps us to understand the nature of transitions in this context.

arxiv-2512-05839.title: Hadronic Emissions from the Microquasar V4641 Sgr, SS433, and its implications in the Diffuse Galactic Emission
arxiv-2512-05839.creator: Debanjan Bose
arxiv-2512-05839.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Debanjan Bose. Microquasars (MQs) are Galactic binary systems, consisting of a star and a compact object, a neutron star or a stellar mass black hole, which accretes matter from its companion star and gives rise to relativistic jets. Recent detection of very-high-energy (VHE; E ≳ 100 ​ GeV E\gtrsim 100\,\text{GeV} ) and ultra-high-energy (UHE; E ≳ 100 ​ TeV E\gtrsim 100\,\text{TeV} ) gamma-rays by LHAASO, HAWC and HESS from the MQ V4641 Sgr and SS 433 suggests them as Galactic PeVatrons.

pmc-10534292.title: Web-Based Self-Compassion Training to Improve the Well-Being of Youth With Chronic Medical Conditions: Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-10534292.creator: Amy Louise Finlay-Jones, Asha Parkinson, Fuschia Sirois, Yael Perry, Mark Boyes, Clare S Rees, Tiffany Leung, Taiane de Azevedo Cardoso, William Collinge, Xuan Zhang
pmc-10534292.description: BackgroundUp to one-third of young people live with chronic physical conditions (eg, diabetes, asthma, and autoimmune disease) that frequently involve recurrent pain, fatigue, activity limitations, stigma, and isolation. These issues may be exacerbated as young people transition through adolescence. Accordingly, young people with chronic illness are at a high risk of psychological distress.

pmc-10675180.title: Additive Manufactured Parts Produced Using Selective Laser Sintering Technology: Comparison between Porosity of Pure and Blended Polymers
pmc-10675180.creator: Chiara Morano, Leonardo Pagnotta, Anton Ficai, Cristina-Elisabeta Pelin
pmc-10675180.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). For different manufacturing processes, porosity occurs in parts made using selective laser sintering (SLS) technology, representing one of the weakest points of materials produced with these processes. Even though there are different studies involving many polymeric materials employed via SLS, and different manuscripts in the literature that discuss the porosity occurrence in pure or blended polymers, to date, no researcher has reported a systematic and exhaustive comparison of the porosity percentage.

pmc-10735583.title: WE CAN WORK IT OUT: NURSING HOME SOCIAL WORK AND CONFLICT MEDIATION
pmc-10735583.creator: Amy Roberts, Nancy Kusmaul, Mercedes Bern-Klug
pmc-10735583.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Drawing from a nationally representative survey of social service directors (N=922), this presentation will provide an overview of nursing home staffing trends and describe the ways in which social service staff routinely interact with residents, families, and staff. Social workers are involved in many aspects of care, including the admissions process, planning and providing care, care transitions, and general supportive services.

pmc-11635354.title: ﻿Number and location of rDNA clusters in the superfamilies Tenthredinoidea and Cynipoidea (Hymenoptera): an update
pmc-11635354.creator: Vladimir E. Gokhman, Valentina G. Kuznetsova, Boris A. Anokhin
pmc-11635354.description: ﻿AbstractTo identify nucleolus organizing regions (NORs), fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) with 18S rDNA probe was performed on chromosomes of Tenthredocampestris Linnaeus, 1758 (Tenthredinidae), Argeciliaris (Linnaeus, 1767) (Argidae) (n = 10 in both) and Aulacideahieracii (Bouché, 1834) (Cynipidae) (2n = 20). In all these species, a single pericentromeric rDNA cluster per haploid karyotype was detected.

pmc-12438345.title: GIS integrated Mental Health Service Delivery Mapping of Korail Slum
pmc-12438345.creator: D T Rashid Soron, K S Azmery, T Consortium
pmc-12438345.description: IntroductionAbout one million people in Bangladesh are living in different slums in Dhaka and Korail is the largest slum of the city with more than 250000 residents. These slums are deprived from most of the basic services and cares such as sanitation, water supply and healthcare. Moreover, the situation related to mental health care might be more disappointing.

pmc-12536623.title: Effect of salicylic acid pretreatment on the postharvest response of hardy kiwifruit during storage
pmc-12536623.creator: Uk Lee, Hyun Ji Eo, Chung Ryul Jung, Yonghyun Kim
pmc-12536623.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Hardy kiwifruit (Actinidia arguta) is a climacteric fruit, a characteristic contributing to its short shelf life. Plant phytohormones such as salicylic acid (SA) are well known for their role in regulating the postharvest fruit ripening processes. Here, we investigated, for the first time, the effect of SA pretreatment on postharvest responses in the hardy kiwifruit cultivar ‘Autumn Sense’ during cold storage.

pmc-12656105.title: Microalgae-Based Biostimulants: Effects on Growth and Stress Resistance in Agricultural Crops
pmc-12656105.creator: Carla Arenas Colarte, Iván Balic, Óscar Díaz, Ignacio Cortes, Adrián A Moreno, Maximiliano J Amenabar, Miguel Castro Retamal, Nelson Caro Fuentes, Daniela Businelli
pmc-12656105.description: Microalgae grow rapidly, require minimal space, can proliferate in non-agricultural land, do not compete with human food sources, and can be cultivated in a variety of environments, including wastewater. They are considered an ecological source of bioactive compounds, offering an environmentally friendly alternative to conventional industrial production methods, which are often resource-intensive.

pmc-12817760.title: Blood pressure response index and acute kidney injury progression in heart failure patients: a retrospective cohort study from MIMIC-IV
pmc-12817760.creator: Baoxin Yan, Xianzhen Cai, Jiating Su, Jinhao Chen, Shuangshuang Tong, Junjun Ye, Weiwen Li, Ying Lin, Xiaojun Huang, Bin Xie, Jilin Li
pmc-12817760.description: BackgroundIn heart failure (HF), acute kidney injury (AKI) is an independent risk factor of mortality, and severer stage of AKI is associated with poorer prognosis. Blood pressure response index (BPRI) reflects the cardiovascular response to vasoactive drugs which are commonly used to increase perfusion to the vital organs.

pmc-13579227.title: Loss of Neutrophils and SLPI Reshapes Early Mucosal Inflammatory Responses During Intranasal Vaccination
pmc-13579227.creator: Oktawia Osiecka, Mariia Tyshchenko, Ivan Sinkevich, Natalia Pocałuń, Joanna Cichy, Jakub M. Kwiecinski, Ewa Oleszycka, Mieszko M. Wilk
pmc-13579227.description: Vaccines delivered via the nasal route have attracted increasing attention for their capacity to engage the mucosal immune system at the primary site of pathogen entry. However, the early innate mechanisms that shape local immune responses following nasal immunisation remain poorly defined. Here, we identified previously uncharacterised tissue‐derived mediators induced during vaccination.
